verificationNotes: Adds a sixth ENCOR Layer3 lab without replacing the existing multi-area, passive or CCNA lessons. Practice has prepared addresses/gateways but no OSPF/static router routes, starts at zero of seventeen tasks and exposes five diagnostic ping actions. The completed reference executes three real IOS command sets, saves startup configuration and serializes empty runtime. It earns twelve live configuration/verification/save tasks after fresh received control state, with no invented traffic or discard evidence.

The guide first omits the range to compare R3’s two unsummarized /24 O IA routes at21/25 against the resulting single /22 at25. It explains source-area ABR placement, preservation of intra-area specifics, maximum-component cost, unused addresses inside a larger aggregate, longest-prefix forwarding and conditional Null0 discard. It distinguishes area range from external summary-address, and explicitly scopes the lab to IPv4 inter-area summarization.

Seventeen tasks cover three router activations with intended addressing/areas/RIDs, passive LAN and P2P cost policy, four Full relationships, the backbone-connected R2 ABR, exact source-area range in a normal OSPF-only domain, retained internal component routes, the remote aggregate without hidden specifics, conditional discard, server return routes, saved healthy policy, four actual ICMP traffic paths and a proved expected failure to an unused address.

A real CLI projection defect selected the first component metric11 for a range instead of maximum15, even though the routing engine correctly installed R3’s metric25. The display now aggregates every matching component, honors explicit cost and most-specific range selection, and reports the received ABR policy snapshot rather than immediately reading changed remote configuration. show ip ospf now derives Active(15), or Passive without reachable components, from received intra-area costs instead of inventing Active(1). These are formatter fixes; the forwarding/SPF engine was already operational and is unchanged.

A regression blocks new protocol89 datagrams after R2 changes its range cost to40. R3 retains its previously received default summary display15 and route25 until delivery resumes; then both update to40/50. Interface enumeration reversal preserves maximum15. Existing OSPFv2/v3 multi-area tests remain compatible with the received-policy projection.

Bounded declarative osum-domain criteria require the intended live areas, passive default, exact active exceptions, normal areas, IPv4 forwarding, only OSPF, no static routes/redistribution/default origination, enabled internal discard and exactly the intended R2 source-area /22 without an explicit cost or suppression option. osum-summary requires the exact selected O IA aggregate, AD110/metric25/next hop/interface, no more-specific route inside the range, and a received ABR router record carrying that range.

Four traffic tasks reuse existing inter-area proof correlating source/target IPv4 ICMP identities, parent-linked replies, every actual forwarding send/receive and currently selected O/O IA routes across the three routers. The expected-failure task requires SRV1’s actual sent request, R3 forwarding via its O IA /22 to R2, R2 receiving and dropping that same request at Null0 using its O summary route, and a delivered ICMP type3 error with the matching parent and quoted addresses. A generic timeout, absent route, disabled discard, bad packet identity, wrong source or wrong quote cannot fabricate this proof. The original request never bounces back toward the backbone.

Tests exercise unsummarized baseline, range on an internal router or wrong source area, a different /23, explicit cost40, not-advertise, static shortcuts, blocked OSPF control and disabled internal discard. Withdrawing only the higher-cost LAN preserves /22 with ABR11/R3 metric21; withdrawing both LAN memberships removes the advertised aggregate and conditional Null0 while transit neighbors remain Full. Restoring membership, intended policy and saved configurations returns healthy traffic and full completion.

IOS write memory and reload restore an unsaved range-cost change. Portable reopening retains genuine traffic and discard observations but requires fresh neighbors, received range policy and aggregate routes before seventeen tasks return. Stable IDs tolerate a hostname change. Imported range/area/identity bounds and missing endpoints fail closed. Existing logical OSPF router records underpin SPF and the Type3 CLI projection; no full scoped binary LSA database, new wire encoder or new live CML capture is claimed.

Final offline Chrome QA covers light/dark at1440/390/320px: actual baseline and summary CLI configuration, unsummarized and aggregate route comparisons, ABR Active15/Type3 metric15, components11/15, four live traffic paths and Windows trace, correlated expected Null0 failure, seventeen tasks, saved offline reload, configuration-only reference, cancel/save-copy protection, responsive fitted topology/guide and unchanged terminal golden styles. Both permalink checks preserve the current host/path/query and workspace and return to ENCOR Layer3 with six labs. Generic catalog QA adds seven checks. All sixteen HTML copies match the final artifact; both desktop diagrams and320px guides were visually inspected. Owned preview returned HTTP200.
